source_text: Habemus etiam vestimentorum in Scripturis mentionem ad spem carnis allegorizare, quia et Apocalypsis Joannis: Hi sunt, ait, qui vestimenta sua non coinquinaverunt cum mulieribus; virgines scilicet significans, et qui semetipsos castraverunt propter regna coelorum. Itaque in albis erunt vestibus, id est, in claritate innubae carnis. Et in Evangelio, indumentum nuptiale sanctitas carnis agnosci potest. Itaque Esaias docens, quale jejunium elegerit Dominus, cum subjicit de mercede bonitatis: Tunc, inquit, lumen tuum temporaneum erumpet, et vestimenta tua citius orientur: non subsericam utique, nec pallium, sed carnem volens accipi, ortum carnis resurrecturae de mortis occasu praedicavit. Adeo nobis quoque suppetit allegorica defensio corporalis resurrectionis. Nam et cum legimus: Populus meus, introite in cellas promas quantulum, donec ira mea praetereat, sepulcra erunt cellae promae, in quibus paulisper requiescere habebunt, qui in finibus saeculi, sub ultima ira, per Antichristi vim excesserint. Aut cur cellarum promarum potius vocabulo usus est, et non alicujus loci receptorii, nisi quia in cellis promis caro salita et usui reposita servatur, depromenda illinc suo tempore? Proinde enim et corpora medicata condimentis sepulturae, mausoleis et monumentis sequestrantur, processura inde cum jusserit Dominus. Quod cum ita intelligi congruat; et quae enim ab ira Dei cellariorum nos refugia servabunt? hoc ipso quod ait, donec ira praetereat, quae extinguet Antichristum, post iram ostendit processuram carnem de sepulcro, in quo ante iram fuerit illata. Nam et de cellariis non aliud effertur, quam quod infertur; et post Antichristi eradicationem agitabitur resurrectio.
pass_a_gloss: We also have a mention of garments in the Scriptures to allegorize the hope of the flesh, because also the Apocalypse of John says: These are, it says, who have not defiled their garments with women; certainly signifying virgins, and those who have castrated themselves for the sake of the heavenly kingdoms. And so they will be in white garments, that is, in the clarity of the flesh's innubation. And in the Gospel, the nuptial garment sanctity of the flesh can be recognized. And so Isaiah, teaching what kind of fast the Lord has chosen, when he adds about the reward of goodness: Then, he says, your temporary light will break forth, and your garments will rise more quickly: certainly not silk or a cloak, but wanting to accept the flesh, he predicted the rise of the flesh of the resurrection from the setting of death. So also an allegorical defense of the bodily resurrection is available to us. For also when we read: My people, enter into your inner rooms for a little while, until my anger passes, the inner rooms will be sepulchers, in which those who have exceeded in the ends of the world, under the last anger, through the power of Antichrist, will rest for a little while. Or why did he use the word of inner rooms rather than some receptive place, unless because in the inner rooms the flesh is salted and preserved for use, to be brought out from there at its own time? Therefore, even the bodies anointed with the spices of burial, are sequestered in sepulchers and monuments, to proceed from there when the Lord commands. Which, when it is understood in this way, also what refuges of storehouses will save us from the anger of God? by this very thing that he says, until the anger passes, which will extinguish Antichrist, after the anger he shows the flesh proceeding from the sepulcher, in which it was brought before the anger. For also from the storehouses nothing else is brought out, than what is brought in; and after the eradication of Antichrist, the resurrection will be set in motion.

pass_b_english: Scripture also mentions garments so we can allegorize the hope of the flesh. The Apocalypse of John says, "These are the ones who have not defiled their garments with women," meaning virgins and those who made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven (Apocalypse of John). Therefore they will wear white robes — that is, they will share in the clarity of the undefiled flesh. In the Gospel, the wedding garment can be recognized as the sanctity of the flesh.

Isaiah, teaching what fast the Lord has chosen, adds a promise about the reward of goodness: "Then your light shall break forth like the dawn, and your healing shall spring up speedily" (Isaiah 58:8). He is not talking about silk or a cloak; by "garments" he means the flesh. He predicts the rising of the resurrection flesh from the sunset of death. So we have an allegorical defense of the bodily resurrection as well.

When we read, "My people, enter your chambers and shut your doors behind you; hide yourselves for a little while until the wrath has passed" (Isaiah 26:20), those chambers are tombs. In them, those who survive to the end of the age under the final wrath through the power of Antichrist will rest briefly. Why does the prophet use the word "chambers" rather than some generic shelter? Because in chambers flesh is salted and stored for later use, to be taken out at its appointed time. Likewise, bodies anointed with burial spices are sealed in tombs and monuments, waiting to come forth when the Lord commands.

If this is the right reading, what storehouse-refuges could save us from God's wrath? The text itself answers: "until the wrath has passed" — the wrath that will destroy Antichrist. After that wrath, the flesh will emerge from the tomb where it was laid before the wrath fell. Nothing comes out of a storehouse except what was put in; and after Antichrist is eradicated, the resurrection will be set in motion.

review.notes: Pass A is a faithful literal translation. Pass B is a fluent rendering that correctly identifies the scripture passages alluded to in the Latin (Isaiah 58:8 and Isaiah 26:20) and provides the required inline citations. The translation of 'innubae' as 'innubation' in Pass A and 'undefiled' in Pass B is acceptable within the bounds of stylistic variation. The translation of 'cellas promas' as 'inner rooms' (A) and 'chambers' (B) is consistent with the Latin. All clauses are accounted for.
